messages:
Maya: Auditor asked for proof that the RBAC change on service-account redwood-ingest actually used the customer KMS key during the incident window. Need a concise bundle: role change audit log, KMS encrypt/decrypt events, and mapping to the deploy commit/id. Can we assemble and export?
Sam: I can query the SIEM for rolebinding changes + KMS events. Will need exact window and affected namespaces. Maya: Window is 2025-11-09 02:00 -> 2025-11-09 04:30 UTC (incident). Affected env = prod-eu and prod-us. We need redaction guidance from auditor for PII in logs.
Oliver: For KMS usage we have CloudKMS logs in cloud-audit.svc. Quick query I run in SIEM:
```
index=cloud_audit action="crypto.*" resource.name="projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/customer-key" earliest="2025-11-09T02:00:00Z" latest="2025-11-09T04:30:00Z"
```
That returns Encrypt/Decrypt/AsymmetricSign events and the caller identity field.
Sam: Good. For RBAC:
```
index=k8s_audit verb="create|update" objectRef.resource=rolebinding namespace="prod-us OR prod-eu" earliest="2025-11-09T01:50:00Z" latest="2025-11-09T05:00:00Z" | stats count by user,objectRef.name,requestURI
```
Maya: Perfect. Auditor asked for a mapping table: rolebinding -> service account -> KMS calls -> commit id. How do we link to commit?
Oliver: The service that triggered the KMS call includes a request metadata header with instance-id. We correlate instance-id to deployment via deploy traces in orchestration logs. Quick join key is instance_id. I can export a CSV with these columns: instance_id, sa_email, rolebinding, kms_event_ts, crypto_action, request_id, deploy_commit_sha.
Jess: Will product/ops sign off on sharing commit SHAs? We might need to redact internal-only metadata.
Maya: AuditorBot, do you have guidance on whether commit SHA and instance IDs are acceptable in evidence?
AuditorBot: Auditor preference: commit SHAs and instance IDs are acceptable if accompanied by a mapping doc that explains their meaning. PII or customer payload must be redacted. We accept logs with replaced emails (e.g., [redacted_email]) and will verify via hashes if needed. Provide checksums of original artifacts.
Sam: Thanks. I started the queries, looks like ~1200 KMS crypto events in window. I'll sample and then export full CSV to S3. Temp export path: s3://redwood-audit-exports/1805006789/
Oliver: I'll drop an export manifest and runbook snippet in the ticket. For S3 copy:
```
aws s3 cp /tmp/evidence-1805006789.csv s3://redwood-audit-exports/1805006789/evidence.csv --acl bucket-owner-full-control
```
Maya: Include sha256 checksums and a short README that declares redaction rules used. Also include the RBAC terraform change (PR link) and the k8s apply job logs that created the binding.
Sam: Noted. Also triage found one suspicious rolebinding created by a CI bot just before the incident. Tagging as vuln-triage item. Will create a vuln ticket with owner.
Jess: Can we also include the escalation timeline so auditor sees operator actions? (pager, bridge calls, incident notes)
Maya: Yes add incident timeline snapshot (ops notes, who ACK'd, mitigation actions).
Oliver: Will attach decryption proof that key usage corresponds to current key version; include KMS key version in export metadata.
Sam: ETA for exports and README: 6 hours. Posting link in ticket when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Maya: Awesome. After upload I'll request auditor access to the s3 prefix via presigned links and ephemeral IAM role.
AuditorBot: Received. Please ensure retention policy on s3 prefix set to 90 days and revoke perms after review. Auditor will ack once artifacts verified. :white_check_mark:
